Let’s be honest: the literature review is usually the part of the dissertation that keeps us up at night. It’s easy to fall into the trap of summarizing papers one by one—it feels like progress, but it’s actually a recipe for a low grade. 

To hit those high marks, you have to shift from 'summarizing' to 'synthesizing.' Here is how I structure my work:

• The Chaotic Method: Writing linear summaries (Avoid this!)
• The Matrix Method: Mapping sources by thematic debates and methodological differences.
• The Result: You stop just reporting facts and start building a narrative that highlights research gaps.

If you’re staring at a mountain of PDFs and don’t know where to start, I’ve put together a template that makes this process ten times faster.
